java_locations.role: Recognizes bracketed link-style clauses within the shaft, maps `hidden` into an invisible LinkType, and still creates and adds the Link event.

Counts bracket-hidden links during semantic single-link classification because `goHidden` does not make `Link.isInvis()` true; an incident hidden link therefore prevents preliminary Opale eligibility.
Serializes a bracket-hidden edge as an ordinary Graphviz edge and solves its route; `isHidden` remains separate from `isInvis` for the later paint layer.
Keeps Graphviz invisibility and paint-layer hidden state as independent semantics; the bracket keyword sets the latter.
Maps the `hidden` style token to the paint-layer `hidden` flag without changing LinkType or Graphviz visibility.
Applies `UHidden.HIDDEN` only while drawing a hidden solved edge, preserving its semantic and layout participation.

rust_locations.role: The shaft scanner rejects `[` before a complete arrow is parsed, so a valid `-[hidden]-` command vanishes instead of producing a connection.
Has no semantic visibility channel, preventing layout and paint from treating one retained relation differently.
All retained connections already participate in layout and UID order, but every connection is counted for Opale incidence and painted because visibility is absent.

claimed_invariant: A valid Deployment `hidden` bracket style creates one explicit paint-hidden DeploymentConnection at the command source line. It retains cleaned endpoints, direction, labels, shaft length and source-order link UID exactly like a visible relation. Unlike Graphviz `style=invis`, the edge is serialized and solved as an ordinary edge and is counted by GraphvizImageBuilder.onlyOneLink, so an incident hidden relation prevents named-note Opale absorption. Only SvekResult's final paint layer suppresses its SVG group, path, arrowhead and label.
causal_divergence: Rust treated the arrow shaft as a flat character run and had no paint-hidden link channel. Encountering the Java bracket style terminates scanning, so the whole command falls through and disappears. That erases an event rather than retaining an ordinary solved edge whose paint is hidden, changing topology, layout constraints, Opale classification and every later global UID.
planned_model_change: Extend Deployment arrow scanning to retain bracket style clauses while deriving arrowhead, direction, line style and length from the bracket-free shaft. Capture whether any style token is `hidden` and store it on DeploymentConnection. Add every hidden edge to layout, solved route matching, semantic Opale incidence and UID allocation exactly like a visible edge, then skip only its final SVG paint phase. Preserve labels and endpoint metadata in the AST even though paint is suppressed.
